I love historical records and origins of holidays so hopefully some of you feel the same way.

Many know that we celebrate thanksgiving on the 4th Thursday of November, but many don't know why. Well the first thanksgiving was actually held more around September 29th. It was a celebration of new provisions from England and many days were designated thanksgiving. The first thanksgiving was in 1621 and lasted for 3 days.

It was 53 pilgrims and 90 native americans. The colonist actually celebrated what they called thanksgiving very regularly as days thanking god for blessings such as military victory, or the end of a drought.

The American holiday origin is the New England Calvinst Thanksgiving. It is Puritan observances and special days set aside during THE week for thanksgiving and praise to god.

A native American named Squanto showed the colonist how to catch eel and grow corn. He even served as in interpreter for them. He learned English as a slave in England. He gave the colonist provisions to survive their first winter as they didn't bring enough provisions with them.

Of the 100 people that arrived on the Mayflower only 50 made it thru that first winter. The day was observed as a day to celebrate the harvest. We don't know the exact date, but we know it was celebrated between Sept. 21st and Nov 11th in 1621. With the most likely time being Sept 21st.

The first thanksgiving was prepared by 4 adult pilgrims

Elenor Billington

Elizabeth Hopkins

Mary Brewster

Susanna White

Along with their young daughters and male as well as female servants.

We know this because two colonist gave personal accounts in historical documents.

The Pilgrims held a true thanksgiving celebration in 1623 following a stretch of rain that was 14 days long. It made their harvest very good. This thanksgiving day was on July 30th in 1623 a Wednesday. It was the day before the supply ship with more colonist arrived. It isn't talked about because it was recognized by civil authority, and not the church. This was likely the first civil recognition of the holiday.

Thanksgiving was celebrated by the Massachusetts Bay Colony in 1630, and frequently thereafter until 1680 when it became an annual festival in the colony.

In the revolutionary war the congress actually appointed one or more thanksgiving days each year because they were not allowed to fight on holidays.

The first national proclamation of thanksgiving was in 1777 by the continental congress from its temporary location in York PA, and it was done there because the British occupied Philadelphia. Samuel Adams created the first draft.

George Washington proclaimed a Thanksgiving in December 1777 as a victory celebration honoring the defeat of the British at Saratoga.

From 1774 to 1789 congress issued several "national days of prayer, humiliation, and thanksgiving". That established American Observances of thanksgiving and National Day of Prayer.

This proclamation was published in The Independent Gazetteer, or the Chronicle of Freedom on Nov 5 1782 being the first observed on Nov 28th of the day.

President John Adams declared Thanksgivings in 1798 and 1799. None were declared by Thomas Jefferson, but James Madison started the tradition again in 1814 in response to resolutions of congress in the war of 1812. He declared the holiday twice in 1815, and none of them were celebrated in autumn.

During the 19th century Thanksgiving varied by celebration from place to place in the USA. Thanksgiving dishes were different as well.

HERE IS WHEN CORPERATE AMERICA CAME INTO PLAY

In 1939 FDR broke the tradition. November had 5 Thursdays that year and this is where we got the 4th Thursday idea. We were in the middle of a depression. FDR "thought" an earlier Thanksgiving would give merchants a longer period to sell goods before Christmas.

At the time adverts for Christmas were deemed inappropriate before thanksgiving.

Fred Lazarus JR was credited with convincing FDR to push Thanksgiving earlier to expand the shopping season. He is the founder of what would be known as Macy's. This didn't go well because republicans denied the change saying it was an affront to the memory of Lincoln.

Many people began to refer to November 30th. The day Lincoln declared thanksgiving during the civil war, and Nov 23rd as Democratic thanksgiving or Franksgiving.

Since a presidential declaration isn't legally binding it was widely dismissed. 23 states went along with it and 22 didn't. Some like Texas however couldn't decide and took both days. lol

In 1940 and 1941 which had 4 Thursdays FDR declared the third one as thanksgiving. As in 1939 some states went with it and other retained the last Thursday idea.

It wasn't until 1942 that congress passed a joint resolution to make it the 4th Thursday in Nov. They passed the amendment in Dec. 26th 1941 they passed it and it was signed in 1942 by FDR.

Some states still didn't recognize the observation. For instance until 1956 Texas celebrated it on the 5th Thursday of Nov when there was.

Hopefully that helps you with some history and enlightened a great many of you.
